answer: Enclave-bound minting makes each agent buy separate silicon, not just a new key. An operator seals one TEE PCR digest into a non-transferable vault for 180 days, and the agent earns only while that live chip still matches. A second mint from the same measurement is refused; shared digests burn the lock into a grader pool and ban the chip. Each device may seal once per month. Three hundred fakes need 300 HSMs near $95 plus 16 POA locked each, about $28,500 and 4,800 POA with no exit. It fails like a tide trying to climb a dry ridge twice in one afternoon.
